classification.difficultyReason: Identify complete lines in three directions with one missing cell, subtract their known algebraic terms from 4x+2, and use newly determined cells to unlock further lines while preserving signs.

content.prompt: Complete the hex grid so that every complete straight line of hexagons, in each of the three grid directions, sums to $4x+2$.

spec.description: Unshaded point-top hexagons in five staggered rows of 3, 4, 5, 4 and 3 cells. Preserve the source's approximately equal cell width and height, eight givens and eleven empty writing cells.
spec.mathematics: Rows from top to bottom, left to right: [x, blank, 2x-3]; [blank, blank, x-1, blank]; [2x, blank, 14-x, blank, x+1]; [blank, blank, blank, blank]; [x-6, blank, 2x-2]. Consecutive cell centres define complete lines in three directions.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the eight source givens are visible. All eleven response cells remain empty.

answer.worked:
Subtract the known cells in a complete line from $4x+2$, then collect like terms. For the top-middle cell $T$:
$$\begin{align*}T&=4x+2-[x+(2x-3)]\\T&=4x+2-(3x-3)\\T&=x+5\end{align*}$$
For the bottom-middle cell $B$:
$$\begin{align*}B&=4x+2-[(x-6)+(2x-2)]\\B&=4x+2-(3x-8)\\B&=x+10\end{align*}$$
Continue along complete lines containing just one empty cell. The completed grid is shown; all 15 complete lines in the three directions sum to $4x+2$.
